person: a best friend who moved away
shape: little things that quietly fix a bad day

slides.text: how a friend who moved away still fixes your worst afternoons
sending a six-minute voice note from the supermarket car park, just so your quiet kitchen has some noise while you unpack groceries.
texting you a photo of an ugly green armchair at a yard sale, because she knows you would have hated it too.
calling on a tuesday evening to say [[put me on speaker]], then washing her own dishes in silence while you fold laundry.
sending three dollars on an app with the note "buy the donut", right after your twelve o'clock meeting went sideways.
mailing a battered paperback with the corner of page eighty turned down, right where the plot gets stupid enough to distract you.
texting [[call me when you walk out]] at ten past two, because she remembered the doctor appointment you only mentioned once.
save this for the long evenings when the map feels too wide, to remember nobody actually left.

caption:
it takes four hours on a train to see my best friend now.
the distance is real, but the way we complain about bad drivers hasn't changed at all.
save this for a slow sunday evening when the flat feels too quiet.
